owasp_tool_projects.status: No dedicated OWASP flagship secrets-detection tool project; OWASP Dependency-Check/ZAP are unrelated. Community references point to third-party OSS (TruffleHog, Gitleaks/Betterleaks, detect-secrets). OWASP Agentic Security Initiative (ASI) Top 10 for Agentic Applications (2025-2026 drafts) is the emerging companion for agent credential risks
owasp_tool_projects.how_team_should_use: Do not expect an OWASP-branded scanner; standardise on Betterleaks or TruffleHog OSS for open-source baselines

market_trends_2025_2026: Secrets sprawl keeps growing: GitGuardian State of Secrets Sprawl 2026 reports 28.65M hardcoded secrets added to public GitHub in 2025 (+34% YoY), 1.28M AI-service secrets (+81% YoY), 113K leaked DeepSeek keys, 24,008 secrets in MCP config files (2,117 valid), Claude Code-assisted commits leaking at 3.2% vs 1.5% baseline, 64% of 2022 credentials still valid in Jan 2026, and ~28% of enterprise incidents originating outside repos (Slack, Jira, Confluence).

NHI convergence and consolidation: secrets scanners rebrand as NHI platforms (GitGuardian $50M Series C Feb 2026, Truffle $25M Series A Nov 2025) while IAM/security majors buy NHI natives (Cisco-Astrix May 2026, SailPoint-Entro June 2026, CrowdStrike-SGNL Feb 2026, Palo Alto-CyberArk Feb 2026, Cyera-Oasis LOI July 2026). Expect fewer standalone NHI vendors by 2027.

Push protection is now the default expectation: GitHub keeps widening default-blocked patterns (June 2026), GitLab push protection GA on Ultimate, and every commercial scanner ships pre-commit/pre-receive blocking. Buyers should treat push protection as table stakes and differentiate on validation, history remediation and collaboration-tool coverage.

Generic secret detection via ML is mainstream: GitHub Copilot secret scanning (GA Oct 2024), Cycode ML engine plus Classifier Agent (2026), Snyk contextual ML (GA Aug 2026), Nightfall LLM detectors, and OSS Betterleaks BPE token-efficiency (Mar 2026). Regex-only tools (Gitleaks, detect-secrets, Spectral) are falling behind on password-style secrets.

AI-agent credential sprawl is the new frontier: GitGuardian AI hooks and agent/MCP inventory (Sept 2026), GitHub MCP Server secret scanning (preview Mar 2026), Nightfall MCP security, Legit VibeGuard/MCP, Doppler and Vault MCP servers for secretless agent access. Controls now need to cover prompt submission, tool-call payloads and per-endpoint agent inventories, not just git.

Validity-only triage is insufficient: GitGuardian reports 46% of critical secrets would be missed by validation-only prioritisation, pushing vendors toward context (blast radius, ownership, lineage) rather than liveness alone.

top_3_recommended_contenders.reasoning: Broadest verified coverage (480+ specific detectors, 19 generic, collaboration tools, containers, endpoints), mature validity/revocation workflows, and the only vendor in this sweep with GA AI-agent hooks plus MCP inventory. Self-hosted option fits regulated clients. Cost and Enterprise-gating are the trade-offs.

For GitHub-standardised clients it delivers push protection, validity checks, AI generic-password detection and MCP-agent scanning at a transparent $19 per active committer with no pipeline changes. Choose it as the primary control when the SCM estate is GitHub and augment with a cross-source scanner for Slack/Jira/containers.

top_3_recommended_contenders.tool: TruffleHog Enterprise (with Cycode as the ASPM alternative)
top_3_recommended_contenders.reasoning: Best verification-first engine (800+ verified types), strong Analyze blast-radius features and the widest OSS-compatible source list at lower cost than GitGuardian; lacks ML generic detection, so pair with Betterleaks or GitHub Copilot detection. Cycode is the pick where the client wants ML generic detection inside an ASPM.

category_notes.best_oss_pick: Betterleaks (drop-in Gitleaks successor, MIT, 98.6% recall claim) for pre-commit and CI blocking, paired with TruffleHog OSS for verification and multi-source historical sweeps. Gitleaks is feature-frozen; detect-secrets is too narrow for greenfield deployments.
